metadata.methodology: Comprehensive entity extraction following EXTRACTION_METHODOLOGY.md guidelines

location.description: peninsula between 43° 46' N. lat., and 61° 67' W. long., connected with New Brunswick by an isthmus about 14 miles wide
location.dimensions: length about 300 miles, breadth about 100 at its widest
location.area_notes: about one-fifth part consists of lakes, rivers, and inlets of the sea

major_cities.name: Halifax
major_cities.description: harbour has an area of about 10 square miles, is open at all seasons, affording safe anchorage for 1,000 ships. British Government has an extensive dockyard

islands.name: Cape Breton
islands.description: separated by the Gut of Canso, forms part of the province

climate.description: remarkably healthy, more temperate than any other part of the Dominion, but fogs prevail on the coast at certain seasons

events.event: taken by the English, grant made to Sir W. Alexander by James I
restored to France, with Quebec, by the treaty of St. Germain-en-laye
ceded to England at the Peace of Utrecht
after the Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle, settlement of disbanded troops formed by Lord Halifax
Cape Breton finally taken from the French
Cape Breton formed a separate colony

executive_council.description: three of whom are departmental heads

legislative_council.appointment: appointed by the Governor for life

education.central_control: Council of Public Instruction—a body identical in membership with the Executive Council of the Province
education.local_management: Board of Trustees chosen by ratepayers (in towns, Town Council or committee)
education.compulsory: between ages of 7 and 12, non-attendance exposes to pecuniary penalties

president_premier.name: Hon. W. S. Fielding
president_premier.title: President of the Council, Premier and Provincial Secretary

aide_de_camp.name: Captain the Hon. J. G. R. U. Colborne
